summary:
Dasgupta, Kakde and Ventullo prove the Gross–Stark conjecture. Let F be a totally real field, χ a totally odd character of G_F cut out by the CM extension H/F, p a prime and E the finite extension of Q_p generated by the values of χ. Partition the primes of F above p into R = {p : χ(p) = 1} and R′, and write r = r_p(χ) = #R. Gross's regulator is R_p(χ) = det(ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1}) ∈ E, where o_p and ℓ_p are the valuation and the p-adic logarithm of the norm on the χ-component U_χ of the p-units of H; Gross's Conjecture 2 is L_p^{(r)}(χω, 0)/(r! L(χ, 0)) = R_p(χ) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p)), for the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function. Theorem 1 proves it: L_an(χ) = R_p(χ). With the known inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r, Gross's Conjecture 1 becomes unconditionally equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0. The rank one case was proved by Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack and Ventullo; the higher rank case had been thought unapproachable by their methods.

The proof. Any class κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) unramified outside R is orthogonal to the p-units: Σ_{i=1}^r (res_{p_i} κ)(u) = 0 for u ∈ U_χ (Proposition 2.1, proved twice, once by Poitou–Tate duality and the Kummer map and once by class field theory alone). In rank one one constructs a cyclotomic class and reads L_an(χ) off its local restriction; for r > 1 the local restriction is no longer injective, and the authors do not know how to construct even one cyclotomic class. Instead they build a class κ with values in a module B̄ and use the orthogonality directly: the r resulting equations make a determinant vanish, and the determinant computes the regulator.

The class comes from Ribet's method. A linear combination of Eisenstein series and Ventullo's auxiliary family gives a cuspidal Hida family F of Hilbert modular forms specializing in weight one to the p-stabilized Eisenstein series E_1(1, χ_S). F is not an eigenform modulo π^{r+1}, so instead of an infinitesimal eigenform the authors study its whole Hecke orbit: the orbit is finite-dimensional over E[π]/π^{r_an+1} and yields Λ-algebra homomorphisms from the Hecke algebra onto explicit local Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3 (Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, one for each of the three cases R′ ≠ ∅; R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) ≠ 0; R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) = 0), in which U_{p_i} ↦ 1 + ε_i and the single relation ε_1 ⋯ ε_r = −(−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} carries the leading term of the p-adic L-function. The Galois representations of Wiles and Hida attached to the Hida eigenfamilies, glued over the reduced localized Hecke algebra, give the cocycle κ(σ) = b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ); Ribet's wrench and the ordinary local shape at p bound it (Lemmas 4.6–4.9), and applying the homomorphism to the vanishing determinant produces, in the one-dimensional space m_W^r/m_W^{r+1}, exactly the identity (−1)^{r+1} L_an(χ) det(o_i(u_j)) + det(ℓ_i(u_j)) = 0, which is Theorem 1. Case 3 needs the same argument run with the lower left entries of the representation in place of the upper right ones, which also fills a hole in the rank one paper (Remark 5.2).

What it needs. Almost nothing here is in the libraries. Mathlib has Dirichlet's unit theorem, the one library item; Tau Ceti has the local Teichmüller lift, the formal logarithm log(1+x) and Chebotarev infrastructure, but not the p-adic logarithm on Q_p^*, the Artin maps, Chebotarev's theorem, Hilbert modular forms, Hida theory or any p-adic L-function. The atlas plans the Deligne–Ribet L-function and the Hilbert Eisenstein series (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3), ordinary theory over totally real fields (PadicFamilies L5), Galois representations over ordinary Hecke algebras (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3), Poitou–Tate duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4) and Wiles's totally real main conjecture (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5), but nothing plans the Gross–Stark conjecture itself.

items.name: The character χ and the field H
items.statement: F is a totally real number field and χ : G_F → Q̄^* a totally odd character of its absolute Galois group, i.e. χ(c_v) = −1 for every complex conjugation c_v. H is the CM cyclic extension of F cut out by χ, the subfield of F̄ fixed by ker χ, and G = Gal(H/F). Embeddings Q̄ ↪ C and Q̄ ↪ C_p are fixed once and for all, so that χ may be read in either C or C_p.
items.note: Totally odd means odd at every archimedean place; H is CM because F is totally real and χ is totally odd, so complex conjugation is a single element c ∈ G independent of the place.

items.name: The Artin L-function L(χ, s) and its Euler factors
items.statement: The complex Artin L-function L(χ, s) of the one-dimensional character χ, its analytic continuation and functional equation, and the convention adopted throughout the paper: χ(p) = 0 if p ramifies in H/F, and χ(p) = χ(Frob(p, H/F)) if p is unramified in H/F.
items.note: Read as the L-function of the associated ray-class character of F; the paper uses only its values at non-positive integers and the vanishing order at s = 0.

items.name: The p-depleted L-function L*(χ, s)
items.statement: L*(χ, s) = L(χ, s) · ∏_{p | p} (1 − χ(p)(Np)^{−s}), the L-function of χ with the Euler factors at the primes above p removed.

items.name: L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 for totally odd χ
items.statement: For χ totally odd, L(χ, 0) ≠ 0. This follows from the functional equation for L(χ, s) together with the non-vanishing L(χ^{-1}, 1) ≠ 0.
items.note: Stated in the paper as well known, with no reference; L(χ, 0) appears in the denominator of both Conjecture 2 and L_an(χ), so the statement is needed for those to be defined.

items.name: The Teichmüller character ω
items.statement: ω : G_F → μ_{p−1} (to μ_2 if p = 2), the Teichmüller character, i.e. the composition of the cyclotomic character with the Teichmüller lift; and ⟨x⟩ = x/ω(x) for x ∈ Z_p^*.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the local Teichmüller lift `TauCeti.teichmuller : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100, read at f790474); the Galois character ω of G_F and the decomposition x = ω(x)⟨x⟩ are not in either library. DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 plans the Teichmüller decomposition of Z_p^*.

items.name: Siegel's algebraicity theorem
items.statement: For n ∈ Z_{≤0} the values L*(χω^n, n) are algebraic, so that by the fixed embedding Q̄ ↪ C_p they may be read as p-adic numbers.
items.note: Attributed to Siegel and used without reference. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans the algebraicity of negative critical values for a totally real field.

items.name: The Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function
items.statement: For χ ≠ ω^{-1} there is a unique meromorphic — indeed analytic — p-adic L-function L_p(χω, s) : Z_p → C_p determined by the interpolation property L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) for n ∈ Z_{≤0}.
items.note: Proved independently by Deligne–Ribet and Cassou-Noguès; the paper also cites the newer constructions of Charollois–Dasgupta, Spiess and Beilinson–Kings–Levin. Neither library has any p-adic L-function of a totally real field.

items.name: The partition R ∪ R′ and the rank r_p(χ)
items.statement: The set of primes of F above p is partitioned as R ∪ R′, where R = {p | p : χ(p) = 1} and R′ = {p | p : χ(p) ≠ 1}; r_p(χ) = #R, written r throughout.
items.note: The primes in R are exactly those whose Euler factor in (2) vanishes at s = 0; the paper writes the empty set as φ, so 'R′ = φ' means R′ = ∅.

items.name: The order of vanishing of L*(χ, s) at s = 0
items.statement: ord_{s=0} L*(χ, s) = r_p(χ), since L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 and r_p(χ) is precisely the number of Euler factors above p in (2) that vanish at s = 0.

items.name: Gross's Conjecture 1 (the order of vanishing)
items.statement: ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) = r_p(χ).
items.note: Not proved in this paper. Theorem 1 makes it unconditionally equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0.

items.name: The inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r_p(χ)
items.statement: ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r_p(χ). For p ≠ 2 this follows from Wiles's proof of the Main Conjecture of Iwasawa theory for totally real fields; an analytic proof valid for all p was given by Charollois–Dasgupta and by Spiess, both resting on Spiess's results on cohomological p-adic L-functions.
items.note: Cited, not proved. IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5 plans Wiles's totally real main conjecture; the deduction of (4) from it (Ventullo §2.1) and the analytic proofs are not planned anywhere.

items.name: Iwasawa's p-adic logarithm
items.statement: log_p : Q_p^* → Z_p, Iwasawa's p-adic logarithm, normalized so that log_p(p) = 0.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the formal logarithm `NormedSpace.logOneAdd` on a normed algebra (TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/LogOneAdd/Basic.lean:66, read at f790474), which gives log on the 1-units; the extension to Q_p^* with log_p(p) = 0 is not there. DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 plans exactly this normalization.

items.name: The local maps o_P and ℓ_P
items.statement: For a prime P of O_H above p, the two continuous homomorphisms o_P = ord_P : H_P^* → Z and ℓ_P = log_p ∘ Norm_{H_P/Q_p} : H_P^* → Z_p.

items.name: The p-units U, the divisor group X and their minus parts
items.statement: U = O_H[1/p]^* is the group of p-units of H and X the free abelian group on the set S_p of primes of O_H above p, both G-modules. Their minus parts for the unique complex conjugation c ∈ G are U^- = {u ∈ U : c(u) = u^{-1}} and X^- = {x ∈ X : c(x) = −x}, and o_p : U^- → X^-, o_p(u) = (o_P(u))_P, ℓ_p : U^- → X^- ⊗ Z_p, ℓ_p(u) = (−ℓ_P(u))_P.
items.note: Note the sign in ℓ_p, which matches the sign in the numerator of (8).

items.name: o_p is a rational isomorphism of Q[G]-modules
items.statement: After tensoring with Q the map o_p induces a Q[G]-module isomorphism U^- ⊗ Q ≅ X^- ⊗ Q.
items.note: Cited to Tate's book on Stark's conjectures, I.4; a form of the Dirichlet S-unit theorem together with the finiteness of the class group.

items.name: The χ-components U_χ and X_χ
items.statement: E is the finite extension of Q_p generated by the values of χ, and U_χ = {u ∈ U^- ⊗ E : σ(u) = u^{χ^{-1}(σ)}}, X_χ = {x ∈ X^- ⊗ E : σ(x) = χ^{-1}(σ)x}. Both are E-vector spaces of dimension r_p(χ), and o_p, ℓ_p induce E[G]-module homomorphisms o_p^χ, ℓ_p^χ : U_χ → X_χ with o_p^χ an isomorphism.

items.name: Gross's p-adic regulator R_p(χ)
items.statement: R_p(χ) = det(ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1}) ∈ E, in parallel with the classical Stark regulator.
items.note: Footnote 1: this normalization differs from the regulator of Gross's paper by the factor (−1)^{r_p(χ)} ∏_{p | p} f_p, and is chosen to agree with Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack.

items.name: Gross's Conjecture 2 (the Gross–Stark conjecture)
items.statement: With r = r_p(χ), L_p^{(r)}(χω, 0) / (r! · L(χ, 0)) = R_p(χ) · ∏_{p ∈ R′} (1 − χ(p)), an equality in E. The statement does not depend on Conjecture 1.

items.name: The p-adic Gamma function
items.statement: Morita's p-adic Gamma function Γ_p and its special values, as used in the Gross–Koblitz and Ferrero–Greenberg theorems.
items.note: Used only through the two cited theorems; not otherwise developed in the paper.

items.name: The Gross–Koblitz formula
items.statement: Gauss sums are expressed in terms of special values of the p-adic Gamma function.
items.note: Cited, not proved; an input to the case F = Q.

items.name: The Ferrero–Greenberg theorem
items.statement: The derivative at s = 0 of a Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function is expressed through special values of the p-adic Gamma function; in particular L_p′(χω, 0) ≠ 0 for χ ≠ 1.
items.note: Cited, not proved; an input to the case F = Q.

items.name: Gross's theorem: Conjectures 1 and 2 for F = Q
items.statement: Both conjectures hold when F = Q; Conjecture 2 follows by combining the Gross–Koblitz formula with the theorem of Ferrero–Greenberg. This special case motivated the general conjecture.

items.name: Federer–Gross: equality of valuations
items.statement: When the order of χ divides p − 1, the p-adic valuations of the two sides of Conjecture 2 are equal; in particular, under that restriction Conjecture 1 is equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0.
items.note: Cited to Federer–Gross, Proposition 3.10, proved there from the Iwasawa Main Conjecture.

items.name: The analytic L-invariant L_an(χ)
items.note: Written with a script L in the paper; distinct from the L-function L_p.

items.name: Theorem 1 — the Gross–Stark conjecture
items.statement: L_an(χ) = R_p(χ). Equivalently, Conjecture 2 holds for every totally odd character χ of the absolute Galois group of a totally real field and every prime p.
items.note: The main theorem of the paper. The rank one case was proved by Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack under hypotheses later removed by Ventullo.

items.name: Conjecture 1 is equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0
items.statement: In view of (4) and Theorem 1, Conjecture 1 holds if and only if R_p(χ) ≠ 0; this is known for r ≤ 1.
items.note: The case r ≤ 1 is Gross, Proposition 2.13, and yields Conjecture 1 for F = Q.

items.name: Remark 1.1 — the characteristic polynomial of the regulator matrix
items.statement: The endomorphism ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1} of U_χ is canonically defined, so one may ask for its characteristic polynomial and not only its determinant. Dasgupta–Spiess conjecture a formula for that characteristic polynomial in terms of the Eisenstein cocycle, generalizing the Gross–Stark conjecture; that conjecture remains open.
items.note: Recorded as context: an open conjecture, not a result of this paper.

items.name: The maps o_i and ℓ_i attached to the primes of R
items.statement: For R = {p_1, …, p_r} and each p_i, o_i = ord_{p_i} : F_{p_i}^* → Z and ℓ_i = log_p ∘ Norm_{F_{p_i}/Q_p} : F_{p_i}^* → Z_p. After choosing a prime P_i of H above p_i the embedding O_H[1/p] ⊂ H ⊂ H_{P_i} ≅ F_{p_i} — an isomorphism because χ(p_i) = 1, so p_i splits completely in H/F — lets o_i and ℓ_i be evaluated on p-units and extended E-linearly to o_i, ℓ_i : O_H[1/p]^* ⊗ E → E.
items.note: The identification H_{P_i} ≅ F_{p_i} is used silently; it holds because p_i ∈ R.

items.name: The regulator as a ratio of determinants
items.statement: For any E-basis u_1, …, u_r of U_χ, R_p(χ) = det(−ℓ_i(u_j))_{i,j} / det(o_i(u_j))_{i,j} ∈ E. The ratio is independent of the basis, and independent of the choice of P_i because replacing P_i by σ(P_i) scales the ith row of both matrices by χ(σ).

items.name: Non-vanishing of det(o_i(u_j))
items.statement: det(o_i(u_j)) ≠ 0: the χ^{-1}-component of the group of p_i-units of H is one-dimensional for each p_i ∈ R, so for a suitable basis {u_i} the matrix (o_i(u_j)) is the identity.
items.note: Deduced in the paper from the Dirichlet unit theorem; the statement actually needed is the S-unit theorem together with the semisimple decomposition of the E[G]-module U ⊗ E.

items.name: Dirichlet's unit theorem
items.statement: For a number field K the unit group of O_K modulo torsion is free of rank r_1 + r_2 − 1 = #{infinite places} − 1.
items.note: Mathlib at 082e2d3: `NumberField.Units.rank` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean:359), with `NumberField.Units.unitLattice_rank` (:385) and `NumberField.Units.finrank_modTorsion` (:458) — the earlier name `rank_modTorsion` is deprecated there. The S-unit theorem the paper needs is a separate item.

items.name: The S-unit theorem with its Galois module structure
items.statement: For S the set of archimedean places of H together with S_p, the group of S-units of H modulo torsion is free of rank #S − 1, and U^- ⊗ Q ≅ X^- ⊗ Q as Q[G]-modules, so that dim_E U_χ = dim_E X_χ = r_p(χ) and the χ^{-1}-component of the p_i-units is one-dimensional.
items.note: Neither library has the S-unit theorem; Mathlib has the case S = ∞ (see the item dirichlet-unit-theorem).

items.name: Compatible decomposition and inertia groups
items.statement: For each place v of F a decomposition group G_v ⊂ G_F is chosen, with inertia subgroup I_v ⊂ G_v; this is an embedding F̄ ⊂ F̄_v and specifies a prime of H above v. For p_i ∈ R the specified prime is the P_i of (7).

items.name: The twisted Galois modules V(χ^{-1}) and V(χ)(1)
items.statement: For an E-vector space V, V(χ^{-1}) is the E[G_F]-module on which σ acts by χ^{-1}(σ); V(χ)(1) is the twist of V(χ) by the cyclotomic character.

items.name: Cohomology unramified outside R
items.statement: H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) ⊂ H^1(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) is the subspace of continuous cohomology classes κ that are unramified outside R, i.e. res_{I_v} κ ∈ H^1(I_v, V(χ^{-1})) is trivial for all v ∉ R.

items.name: The local cohomology at a prime of R
items.statement: For p_i ∈ R one has χ(G_{p_i}) = 1, so H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ^{-1})) = H^1(G_{p_i}, E) = Hom_cts(G_{p_i}, E) ≅ Hom_cts(F̂_{p_i}^*, E), the last isomorphism by local class field theory.

items.name: The local reciprocity map, in Serre's normalization
items.statement: The local Artin map rec_{p_i} : F̂_{p_i}^* → G_{p_i}^{ab} on the profinite completion F̂_{p_i}^* = lim_m F_{p_i}^*/(F_{p_i}^*)^m, normalized as in Serre's Corps locaux: for u ∈ O_{F_p}^*, ε_cyc(rec(u)) = Norm_{O_{F_p}/Z_p} u, and rec(ϖ^{-1}) lifts the Frobenius of the maximal unramified extension for a uniformizer ϖ.
items.note: The normalization is stated in a footnote and matters for every sign in §5. Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans the absolute local Artin map and its normalizations at Layer 7; neither library has it at f790474.

items.name: o_i and ℓ_i as characters of the profinite completion
items.statement: o_i and ℓ_i are continuous for the topology on F_{p_i}^* defined by the subgroups (F_{p_i}^*)^m, so they induce continuous homomorphisms o_i : F̂_{p_i}^* → Ẑ → Z_p and ℓ_i : F̂_{p_i}^* → Z_p.

items.name: The cyclotomic subspace H^1_cyc(χ)
items.statement: H^1_cyc(χ) ⊂ H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})) is the set of κ such that for each p_i ∈ R the restriction res_{p_i} κ ∈ H^1(G_{p_i}, E) lies in the E-span of o_i and ℓ_i, viewed as continuous homomorphisms F̂_{p_i}^* → E.

items.name: dim_E H^1_cyc(χ) = r
items.statement: The space of cyclotomic classes has dimension r over E.
items.note: The paper calls this a straightforward generalization of Lemma 1.5 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack and gives no proof; it is used for the definition of L_alg(χ) and for det(y_ij) ≠ 0.

items.name: The algebraic L-invariant L_alg(χ)
items.statement: For a basis κ_1, …, κ_r of H^1_cyc(χ) write res_{p_j} κ_i = x_ij o_j + y_ij ℓ_j with x_ij, y_ij ∈ E. Then L_alg(χ) = det(x_ij)/det(y_ij), after Greenberg's study of exceptional zeroes.

items.name: Non-vanishing of det(y_ij)
items.statement: det(y_ij)_{i,j=1…r} ≠ 0, using the linear independence of κ_1, …, κ_r together with dim_E H^1_cyc(χ) = r.
items.note: Asserted without proof.

items.name: Proposition 1 = Proposition 2.1 (orthogonality)
items.statement: Let κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) and u ∈ U_χ. Viewing u as an element of F̂_{p_i}^* ⊗ E via (7), Σ_{i=1}^r (res_{p_i} κ)(u) = 0.
items.note: The engine of the whole proof; two proofs are given in §2.

items.name: L_alg(χ) = R_p(χ)
items.statement: The orthogonality of Proposition 1 implies L_alg(χ) = R_p(χ).
items.note: Asserted as an easy consequence ('one readily proves'), with no computation given. It is not used in the proof of Theorem 1, which computes with the class κ directly.

items.name: The rank one strategy and its obstruction
items.statement: When r = 1 and R = {p}, Conjecture 2 is equivalent to the existence of a nonzero class κ ∈ H^1_cyc(χ) with res_p κ = L_an(χ) o_p + ℓ_p, which is what Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack and Ventullo construct. That construction relies on the injectivity of the local restriction H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})) → H^1(G_p, E) for R = {p}, which fails in general for a fixed p ∈ R when r > 1; the authors do not know how to construct even one cyclotomic class in the general case, and believe the analogous inclusion x_i B ⊂ m to be false for r ≥ 3.
items.note: Recorded because it fixes what the new method must avoid. Footnote 4 adds that if r = 2 and F_{p_i} ≅ Q_p for i = 1, 2 then (11) is injective and a proof in the style of [5] is possible.

items.name: The Kummer isomorphisms δ and δ_v
items.statement: Hilbert's Theorem 90 yields isomorphisms δ : (H^* ⊗̂ E)_{χ^{-1}} ≅ H^1(G_F, E(χ)(1)) and, locally, δ_v : (H_w^* ⊗̂ E)_{χ^{-1}} ≅ H^1(G_v, E(χ)(1)), where H^* ⊗̂ E = (lim_n (H^* ⊗ O_E/p^n)) ⊗_{O_E} E.
items.note: Cited to Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, Proposition 1.4. The paper says explicitly that in Proof 1 'we state without proof certain identifications that are needed'.

items.name: δ identifies U_χ with H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1))
items.statement: Defining H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1)) as the classes whose restriction at each v ∉ R lies in the image of (O_{H,w}^* ⊗̂ E)_{χ^{-1}} under δ_v, the map δ induces an isomorphism δ : U_χ ≅ H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1)).

items.name: Local Tate duality at the primes of R
items.statement: For each p_i ∈ R there is a perfect pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{p_i} : H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ)(1)) × H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ^{-1})) → E.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 plans local duality and its rational-coefficient versions; neither library has continuous Galois cohomology duality at the pinned commits.

items.name: Poitou–Tate orthogonality of the restricted subspaces
items.statement: The images of H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) and H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1)) under the product of the restriction maps res_{p_i} are orthogonal under the sum of the local Tate pairings ⟨ , ⟩_R : ∏_i H^1(G_{p_i}, V(χ^{-1})) × ∏_i H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ)(1)) → V.
items.note: Deduced from Poitou–Tate duality, which R02.4 plans together with the nine-term exact sequence. The paper states it without proof.

items.name: Compatibility of the Tate pairing with evaluation
items.statement: ⟨κ, δ(u)⟩_{p_i} = (res_{p_i} κ)(u) for κ ∈ H^1(G_{p_i}, V(χ^{-1})) and u ∈ U_χ.
items.note: One of the identifications stated without proof in Proof 1; it is what makes the abstract duality statement compute the numbers of Proposition 1.

items.name: The restriction of κ to G_H and its equivariance
items.statement: For κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})), res_H κ ∈ H^1(G_H, V(χ^{-1}))^G = Hom_cts(G_H, V)^{χ^{-1}}, the space of continuous homomorphisms f : G_H → V with f(σhσ^{-1}) = χ^{-1}(σ) f(h) for σ ∈ G_F, h ∈ G_H; and res_H κ is trivial on I_w for every place w of H not above a place of R.

items.name: Global class field theory for the ray class field K
items.statement: K is the maximal abelian extension of H unramified outside R_H, and class field theory gives rec : A_H^* / H^* ∏_{w ∉ R_H} O_{H,w}^* ≅ Gal(K/H), with the convention O_{H,w}^* = C^* at a complex place.
items.note: Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans global Artin reciprocity at Layer 11 and class fields at Layer 13; neither library has them at f790474.

items.name: Proof 2 of Proposition 2.1 by class field theory
items.statement: For u an R_H-unit of H, the idèle π_u with component u at each w ∈ R_H and 1 elsewhere is trivial in the quotient (24), so 0 = (res_H κ)(rec(π_u)) = Σ_{w ∈ R_H} (res_w κ)(u) = Σ_{i=1}^r Σ_{σ ∈ G} (res_{σ(P_i)} κ)(u). Using res_{σ(P_i)}(u) = χ^{-1}(σ) res_{P_i}(σ^{-1}(u)) and res_{P_i} = res_{p_i} gives Σ_i (res_{p_i} κ)(u_χ) = 0 for u_χ = Σ_σ σ(u) ⊗ χ(σ), and such u_χ generate U_χ.
items.note: This second proof uses only class field theory and is self-contained; the first needs the unproved identifications above.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (injectivity of the product of inertia restrictions)
items.statement: For an E-vector space V the restriction map ∏_{i=1}^r res_{I_{p_i}} : H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) → ∏_{i=1}^r H^1(I_{p_i}, V) is injective.
items.note: Equivalently: there is no nonzero everywhere-unramified class. This is the substitute for the rank one injectivity (11) that fails for r > 1; it is used in Lemma 4.8.

items.name: res_H is an isomorphism on χ^{-1}-parts
items.statement: res_H : H^1(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) → H^1(G_H, V)^{χ^{-1}} is an isomorphism, because the neighbouring terms in the inflation–restriction sequence are H^i(G, V(χ^{-1})) for i = 1, 2, which vanish as G is finite and V is a torsion-free E-vector space.

items.name: Finiteness of the Hilbert class field
items.statement: The maximal abelian unramified extension of H is a finite extension of H, so a continuous homomorphism from its Galois group to a torsion-free E-vector space vanishes.
items.note: Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans the Hilbert class field at Layer 13.

items.name: Λ, the specializations ν_k and the uniformizer π
items.statement: Λ = O_E[[T]]; for k ∈ Z_p the specialization ν_k : Λ → O_E is the O_E-algebra map T ↦ u^{k−1} − 1 for a fixed topological generator u of 1 + 2pZ_p (u = 1 + p for p odd, u = 5 for p = 2), so that weight 1 is the augmentation T ↦ 0. Λ_{(1)} is the localization at (T) = ker ν_1, a DVR in which p is invertible, with uniformizer π = T / log_p u.

items.name: π translates orders of vanishing into the weight variable
items.statement: If h ∈ Λ_{(1)} is written h = π^n h_0 with h_0 ∈ Λ_{(1)}^*, and f(k) = ν_k(h) on a small neighbourhood of 1 in Z_p, then f has a zero of order n at k = 1 and f^{(n)}(1)/n! = ν_1(h_0).
items.note: This is why π-adic orders in §5 compute derivatives of p-adic L-functions at weight 1.

items.name: The Λ-adic cyclotomic character
items.statement: ε : G_F → Λ^* is the character with ν_k(ε(σ)) = ⟨ε_cyc(σ)⟩^{k−1} for all k ∈ Z_p, given explicitly by ε(σ) = (1 + T)^{log_p⟨ε_cyc(σ)⟩ / log_p u}, where ε_cyc : G_F → Z_p^* is the cyclotomic character.

items.name: Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms and Hida families
items.statement: M(n, χ) is the Λ-module of Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms for F of tame level n = cond(χ) and character χ, with ν_k(F) ∈ M_k(np, χω^{1−k}) for k ≥ 2, S(n, χ) its cuspidal submodule, and Hecke operators T_l for l ∤ np and U_l for l | p. With the ordinary projector e = lim_n (∏_{p | p} U_p)^{n!}, the spaces of Hida families are M^o(n, χ) = eM(n, χ) and S^o(n, χ) = eS(n, χ), and T̃ and T are the Λ-algebras of Hecke operators acting on them.
items.note: Conventions are taken from Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack §§2–3 and Ventullo. PadicFamilies L5 plans ordinary theory over totally real fields and L0a the profinite ordinary projector; neither library has Hilbert modular forms at the pinned commits.

items.name: The Hilbert Eisenstein series E_k(1, η)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1 and η a narrow ray class character of F of modulus b whose parity agrees with k, and excluding F = Q, k = 2, b = 1, the Eisenstein series E_k(1, η) has normalized Fourier coefficients c(a, E_k(1, η)) = Σ_{r | a, (r,b)=1} η(r) Nr^{k−1} and, if b ≠ 1 or k ≠ 1, constant coefficients c_λ(0, E_k(1, η)) = 2^{−[F:Q]} L_b(η, 1−k) for λ ∈ Cl^+(F); when b = 1 and k = 1 the constant coefficients are 2^{−[F:Q]}(L(χ, 0) + χ^{-1}(λ) L(χ^{-1}, 0)).
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans the Hilbert Eisenstein series, the integral q-expansion principle and the constant-term argument. The b = 1, k = 1 constant term is the source of the extra term in Case 2 and Case 3.

items.name: The Eisenstein Hida family E(1, χ)
items.statement: There is E(1, χ) ∈ M^o(n, χ) with ν_k(E(1, χ)) = E_k(1, χω^{1−k}) for all k ≥ 1, where the character χω^{1−k} always has modulus divisible by all primes above p; its constant coefficients are 2^{−[F:Q]} L_p(χω, 1−k).
items.note: This is the bridge between the p-adic L-function and the Hecke action; χ_S denotes χ with modulus divisible by all primes of S.

items.name: Lemma 3.1 (Ventullo): the auxiliary family G
items.statement: There is a Hida family G ∈ M^o(1, ω^{-1})_{(0)} with ν_0(G) = 1 and c_λ(0, G) = 1 for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F). Write G_k = ν_k(G) ∈ M_k(p, ω^{-k}).
items.note: Proved in Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack under Leopoldt's conjecture using Eisenstein series, and unconditionally by Ventullo (his Theorem 2); cited, not reproved here.

items.name: The forms F_k
items.statement: In Case 1 (R′ ≠ ∅), F_k = E_k(1, χω^{1−k}) − E_1(1, χ_{R′}) · G_{k−1} · L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ_{R′}, 0), where L(χ_{R′}, 0) = L(χ, 0) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p)); if R′ = ∅, F_k = E_k(1, χω^{1−k}) − E_1(1, χ) · G_{k−1} · L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ, 0) + E_k(χ, ω^{1−k}) · (L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ, 0)) · (L(χ^{-1}, 0)/L_p(χ^{-1}ω, 1−k)). In both cases F_k ∈ M_k(np, χω^{1−k}) has constant terms equal to 0.

items.name: The Λ-adic families F̃ and the element W
items.statement: With L(χω) ∈ Λ_{(1)} the element with ν_k(L(χω)) = L_p(χω, 1−k): in Case 1 F̃ = E(1, χ) − E_1(1, χ_{R′}) G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1) · L(χω)/L(χ_{R′}, 0); if R′ = ∅, F̃ = E(1, χ) − E_1(1, χ) · G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1) · L(χω)/L(χ, 0) + E(χ, 1) · W, where W = (L(χω)/L(χ^{-1}ω)) · (L(χ^{-1}, 0)/L(χ, 0)) ∈ Frac(Λ) satisfies ν_k(W) = (L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ, 0)) · (L(χ^{-1}, 0)/L_p(χ^{-1}ω, 1−k)) whenever L_p(χ^{-1}ω, 1−k) ≠ 0. In both cases ν_k(F̃) = F_k for positive integers k near 1, using ν_k(G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1)) = ν_{k−1}(G(T)).

items.name: Semi-cusp forms
items.statement: F̃ has vanishing constant coefficients at ∞ — in Ribet's terminology it is a semi-cusp form — but is not yet cuspidal.

items.name: The trichotomy of cases
items.statement: ord_π W = r_an(χ) − r_an(χ^{-1}), and F̃ is regular in weight 1 (i.e. F̃ ∈ M^o(n, χ)_{(1)}) unless W has a pole there. Since swapping χ and χ^{-1} inverts W, one may assume ord_π W ≥ 0. Case 1: R′ ≠ ∅. Case 2: R′ = ∅ and ν_1(W) ≠ 0, where one must prove R_p(χ) = L_an(χ). Case 3: R′ = ∅ and ν_1(W) = 0, where one must prove R_p(χ) = L_an(χ) = 0 and R_p(χ^{-1}) = L_an(χ^{-1}).

items.name: Theorem 3.2: F is a cuspidal Hida family
items.statement: There is a Hecke operator t ∈ T̃_{(1)} such that F = t · e · F̃ is a cuspidal Hida family, F ∈ S^o(n, χ)_{(1)}.
items.note: Cited to Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, Corollary 2.10 and Proposition 3.4; not reproved.

items.name: r_an and the analytic invariant L*_an(χ)
items.statement: r_an = r_an(χ) = ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) and L*_an(χ) = L_p^{(r_an)}(χ, 0) / (r_an! · L(χ, 0) · ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p))). Conjecture 1 states r_an = r, whence L*_an(χ) = L_an(χ), but that is not assumed.
items.note: The published text writes L_p^{(r_an)}(χ, 0) in this display where L_p^{(r_an)}(χω, 0) is meant; see the source issues.

items.name: A Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion
items.statement: There is a canonical Λ-algebra embedding c : S^o(n, χ)_{(1)} → ∏_{a ⊂ O_F} Λ_{(1)}, H ↦ (c(a, H))_a.
items.note: The Λ-adic q-expansion principle for Hilbert modular forms, used to define the Hecke orbit module H; stated without reference.

items.name: The Hecke orbit module H and the homomorphism ϕ
items.statement: H is the image of the Hecke orbit of F under the reduction of c modulo π^{r_an+1}, a finitely generated module over Λ_{(1)}/π^{r_an+1} = E[π]/π^{r_an+1}, and ϕ : T → End_{E[π]/π^{r_an+1}} H is the resulting canonical Λ-algebra homomorphism.
items.note: The key idea, drawn from Ventullo: F need not be an eigenform modulo π^{r+1}, but its Hecke orbit is finite-dimensional and computable.

items.name: Theorem 2 = Theorem 3.3 (the homomorphism in Case 1)
items.statement: Suppose R′ ≠ ∅ and R = {p_1, …, p_r}. There is a Λ-algebra homomorphism ϕ : T → W_1 = E[π, ε_1, …, ε_r]/(π^{r_an+1}, ε_i^2, ε_i π, ε_1 ε_2 ⋯ ε_r + (−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an}) with T_l ↦ 1 + χε(l) for l ∤ np, U_l ↦ 1 for l | n or l ∈ R′, and U_{p_i} ↦ 1 + ε_i. W_1 is a local ring with maximal ideal (π, ε_1, …, ε_r).
items.note: This is where the p-adic L-function enters: the relation ε_1 ⋯ ε_r = −(−1)^{r_an}L*_an(χ)π^{r_an} encodes its leading term.

items.name: The Eisenstein congruence for the second term of F̃
items.statement: π^{r_an} exactly divides L(χω) in Λ_{(1)}, so, since ν_0(G) = 1, F′ = E_1(1, χ_{R′}) G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1) L(χω)/L(χ_{R′}, 0) ≡ (−1)^{r_an} E_1(1, χ_{R′}) L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} (mod π^{r_an+1}), a congruence of Fourier coefficients; hence for τ ∈ T̃, τF′ ≡ (−1)^{r_an} ν_1(τ)(E_1(1, χ_{R′})) L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} (mod π^{r_an+1}), so modulo π^{r_an+1} the Hecke action on F′ only depends on the action on E_1(1, χ_{R′}).

items.name: The Hecke action on the weight one Eisenstein series
items.statement: T_l E_1(1, χ_{R′}) = (1 + χ(l)) E_1(1, χ_{R′}) for l ∤ np and U_l E_1(1, χ_{R′}) = E_1(1, χ_{R′}) for l | n or l ∈ R′; and more generally, for R′ ⊂ J ⊂ S_p and p ∈ S_p, (U_p − 1) E_1(1, χ_J) = E_1(1, χ_{J ∪ {p}}) if p ∉ J and 0 if p ∈ J.
items.note: Called 'a direct calculation'. This is the interesting phenomenon that produces the nilpotents ε_i.

items.name: The relations ε_i^2 = 0 and ε_i π = 0
items.statement: For p_i ∈ R the operator U_{p_i} − 1 annihilates E(1, χ), so π annihilates the image of (U_{p_i} − 1)F in H and the image of (U_{p_i} − 1)^2 F is 0; writing ε_i for the image of U_{p_i} − 1 under ϕ, ε_i^2 = 0 and ε_i π = 0 for all i.

items.name: The product relation
items.statement: ∏_{i=1}^r (U_{p_i} − 1) F ≡ (−1)^{r_an+1} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} F (mod π^{r_an+1}), hence ε_1 ⋯ ε_r + (−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} = 0 in End_{E[π]/π^{r_an+1}} H.

items.name: W_1 has dimension 2^r + r_an − 1 and ϕ(T) ⊗ E ≅ W_1
items.statement: W_1 is generated as an E-vector space by 1, π, …, π^{r_an−1} and the products ∏_{j ∈ J} ε_j over nonempty J ⊂ R, so dim_E W_1 = 2^r + r_an − 1; these elements act E-linearly independently on F, because π^i F vanish to distinct orders less than r_an at k = 1 and the forms ∏_{j ∈ J} ε_j F are congruent, up to nonzero scalars, to E_1(1, χ_{R′ ∪ J}) π^{r_an} modulo π^{r_an+1}. Hence the surjection W_1 → ϕ(T) ⊗_{O_E} E is an isomorphism.
items.note: The linear independence of the E_1(1, χ_J) for distinct J is asserted as 'easily seen'.

items.name: Remark 3.4: the subalgebra T′ and the simpler homomorphism φ′
items.statement: Let T′ ⊂ T be the Λ-subalgebra generated by T_l for l ∤ np, U_l for l | n or l ∈ R′, and U_J = T^{r−#J} ∏_{p ∈ J}(U_p − 1) for nonempty J ⊂ R. The images of these operators under ϕ lie in the E-subalgebra of W_1 generated by π, so restricting ϕ to T′ and reducing modulo π^{r+1} gives φ′ : T′ → E[π]/π^{r+1} with T_l ↦ 1 + χε(l), U_l ↦ 1, U_J ↦ 0 for ∅ ≠ J ⊊ R and U_R ↦ (−1)^{r+1} L_an(χ) π^r; this holds even if r_an > r, in which case L_an(χ) = 0. The map φ′ can be constructed directly from the mod π^{r+1} eigenvalues of F, τF ≡ φ′(τ)F (mod π^{r+1}), and suffices for the applications in §5.
items.note: Only the images of the operators of T′ are needed to expand the determinant in (85) and obtain (87); ϕ on the full Hecke algebra is included for completeness.

items.name: Remark 3.5: the case r = 1 recovers Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack
items.statement: If r = 1 there is a natural Λ_{(1)}-algebra homomorphism W_1 → E[π]/π^2 sending ε_1 ↦ L_an(χ)π, valid even when r_an > r = 1 (then L_an(χ) = 0); composing ϕ with it gives exactly the homomorphism constructed in Case 1 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack.

items.name: Theorem 3.6 (the homomorphism in Case 2)
items.statement: Suppose R′ = ∅ and ν_1(W) ≠ 0. With W_2 = E[π, ε_1, …, ε_r, y]/I_{W_2}, where I_{W_2} = (π^{r_an+1}, y^{r_an+1}, y(π − y), π^{r_an} W − y^{r_an}(W + 1), ε_i^2, ε_i π, ε_i y, ε_1 ε_2 ⋯ ε_r + (−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ)(π^{r_an} − y^{r_an})), there is a Λ-algebra homomorphism ϕ : T → W_2 with T_l ↦ 1 + χε(l) + (χ(l) − 1)((1 − ε(l))/π) y for l ∤ np, U_l ↦ 1 + ((ε(l) − 1)/π) y for l | n, and U_{p_i} ↦ 1 + ε_i.

items.name: The auxiliary operator Y
items.statement: For a fixed prime q ∤ np with χ(q) ≠ 1, Y = (T_q − 1 − χε(q)) / ((χ(q) − 1)(1 − ε(q))/π) ∈ T̃_{(1)}; it satisfies Y F̃ ≡ π E(χ, 1) W (mod π^{r_an+1}) and Y E(χ, 1) = π E(χ, 1).
items.note: Called an explicit computation. Y is what detects the extra Eisenstein term E(χ,1)·W that appears when R′ = ∅.

items.name: The relations in Case 2
items.statement: Modulo π^{r_an+1}: T_l F ≡ (1 + χε(l) + (χ(l) − 1)((1 − ε(l))/π) Y) F for l ∤ np; U_l F ≡ (1 + ((ε(l) − 1)/π) Y) F for l | n; (πY − Y^2)F ≡ 0; Y^{r_an+1} F ≡ 0; (π^{r_an} W − Y^{r_an}(W + 1)) F ≡ 0; (U_p − 1)^2 F ≡ π(U_p − 1) F ≡ 0; (U_p − 1) Y F ≡ 0; and ∏_{i=1}^r (U_{p_i} − 1) F ≡ (−1)^{r_an+1} L*_an(χ)(π^{r_an} − Y^{r_an}) F. The computation of the fifth uses E(1, χ) ≡ E(χ, 1) ≡ E_1(1, χ_S) (mod π).

items.name: dim_E W_2 = 2^r + 2 r_an − 2 and the injectivity in Case 2
items.statement: W_2 is generated as an E-vector space by 1, π, …, π^{r_an−1}, y, y^2, …, y^{r_an} and the products ε_J = ∏_{j ∈ J} ε_j for ∅ ≠ J ⊊ R, so dim_E W_2 = 2^r + 2 r_an − 2; the surjection W_2 → ϕ(T) ⊗_{O_E} E is injective, by a dimension count that treats ν_1(W) ≠ −1 and ν_1(W) = −1 separately and uses ν_1(F) = (1 + ν_1(W)) E_1(1, χ_S) and π^{r_an−1} Y F ≡ π^{r_an} E_1(1, χ_S) ν_1(W) ≢ 0.
items.note: This is the only place the hypothesis ν_1(W) ≠ 0 of Case 2 is used; the construction of the surjection (49) does not need it.

items.name: Remark 3.7: the case r = 1 in Case 2
items.statement: If r = 1 and w = ν_1(W) ≠ 0, −1, the homomorphism W_2 → E[π]/π^2 with y ↦ πw/(w+1) and ε ↦ L_an(χ)π/(w+1) composes with ϕ to give T → E[π]/π^2 with T_l ↦ 1 + χ(l) + ((χ(l) + w)/(1 + w)) log⟨Nl⟩ T, U_l ↦ 1 for l | n and U_p ↦ 1 + (L_an/(1+w)) T — exactly the homomorphism constructed in Case 2 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack.

items.name: Theorem 3.8 (the homomorphism in Case 3)
items.statement: Suppose R′ = ∅ and W has a zero of order s − t ≥ 1, where s = r_an(χ) and t = r_an(χ^{-1}). With W_3 = E[π, ε_1, …, ε_r, y]/I_{W_3}, I_{W_3} = (π^{s+1}, y^{t+1}, y(π − y), π^t W − y^t, ε_i^2, ε_i π, ε_i y, ε_1 ε_2 ⋯ ε_r + (−1)^s L*_an(χ) π^s), there is a Λ-algebra homomorphism ϕ : T → W_3 with the same formulas as in Theorem 3.6.
items.note: The proof of Theorem 3.6 constructs the surjection (49) without using ν_1(W) ≠ 0; when ν_1(W) = 0 it is not injective, and factors through the quotient W_3 because Y^{t+1} F ≡ 0 and Y^t F̃ ≡ π^t W F̃ (mod π^{s+1}).

items.name: Injectivity of W_3 → ϕ(T) ⊗ E
items.statement: The forms {π^i F}_{i=0}^{s} ∪ {Y^i F}_{i=1}^{t−1} ∪ {∏_{j ∈ J}(U_{p_j} − 1) F}_{J ⊂ R, J ≠ ∅, R} are E-linearly independent modulo π^{s+1}.
items.note: 'The demonstration of this fact is similar to the previous cases and left to the reader'; see the source issues. It is what makes Theorem 3.8, hence Case 3, complete.

items.name: The prime m and the local Hecke algebra
items.statement: W denotes W_1, W_2 or W_3 in Cases 1, 2, 3, with maximal ideal m_W, and m ⊂ T is the kernel of the composition T → W → W/m_W ≅ E; m is a height one prime generated by T ∈ Λ, T_l − (1 + χε(l)) for l ∤ np and U_l − 1 for l | np. T_{(m)} is the localization and L = Frac(T_{(m)}) its total ring of fractions.

items.name: T_{(m)} is reduced and L is a product of fields
items.statement: Since the tame character χ has conductor equal to the tame level n, there are no n-old forms, so T_{(m)} is reduced; hence there is a canonical injection T_{(m)} ↪ L ≅ ∏_{i=1}^t L_{H_i}, where each L_{H_i} is a finite extension of Frac(Λ) corresponding to a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily H_i.
items.note: The paper stresses that this observation was missing from Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, thanks Hida for pointing it out, and refers to Hida's 1988 Annals paper, proof of Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7, pp. 381–382.

items.name: The Hecke algebra of an eigenfamily and its congruences
items.statement: For an integral ideal a, c(a, H_i) ∈ L_{H_i} is the image of T_a; these coefficients generate a finite local Λ-subalgebra Λ_{H_i} ⊂ L_{H_i}, the image of T_{(m)} in L_{H_i} is the localization of Λ_{H_i} at a height one prime m_{H_i} above (T) ⊂ Λ, and c(l, H_i) ≡ 1 + χ(l) (mod m_{H_i}) for l ∤ np, c(l, H_i) ≡ 1 (mod m_{H_i}) for l | np — i.e. the specialization of H_i at m_{H_i} is the weight one form E_1(1, χ_S).

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (Hida, Wiles): Galois representations of Hida families
items.statement: For a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily H specializing at a weight one prime m_H ⊂ Λ_H to E_1(1, χ_S), there is a continuous irreducible Galois representation ρ_H : G_F → GL_2(L_H), for L_H = Frac(Λ_H) with the Λ-adic topology, such that (1) ρ_H is unramified outside np; (2) for l ∤ np, char(ρ_H(Frob_l))(x) = x^2 − c(l, H) x + χε(l); (3) for all p | p, ρ_H|_{G_p} is reducible with semisimplification χ ε η_p,H^{-1} ⊕ η_p,H, where η_p,H : G_p → Λ_H^* is unramified with η_p,H(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = c(p, H) for a uniformizer ϖ ∈ F_p^*.
items.note: Cited to Wiles's 1988 Inventiones paper, Theorems 2 and 4. OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3 plans the Galois representation over the ordinary Hecke algebra together with its ordinary local structure, including the residually reducible case.

items.name: Integrality and reduction of characteristic polynomials
items.statement: char(ρ_H(σ))(x) ∈ Λ_H[x] for all σ ∈ G_F, and char(ρ_H(σ))(x) ≡ (x − 1)(x − χ(σ)) (mod m_H); both follow from (51), (52) by Chebotarev and the continuity of ρ_H, using that Λ_H and m_H are finitely generated Λ-modules and hence closed in the Λ-adic topology.

items.name: Chebotarev's density theorem
items.statement: The Frobenius elements Frob_l, for l ranging over the primes unramified in a Galois extension, are dense in the Galois group.
items.note: Used three times, to spread a statement about Frobenius elements to all of G_F. Tau Ceti has Chebotarev infrastructure at f790474 — `NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean:93) and the auxiliary-prime and prime-counting files — but not the density theorem, which its Chebotarev roadmap plans at Layers 9–10.

items.name: Diagonalizing ρ_H(τ)
items.statement: For τ ∈ G_F with χ(τ) ≠ 1, Hensel's lemma applied to (55) gives distinct eigenvalues λ_1, λ_2 ∈ Λ_{m_H} of ρ_H(τ) with λ_1 ≡ 1 and λ_2 ≡ χ(τ) modulo m̂_H, where Λ_{m_H} is the completion of the localization of Λ_H at m_H; after extending scalars to L_{m_H} one may choose a basis of eigenvectors, so that ρ_H(τ) = diag(λ_1, λ_2).

items.name: Ribet's wrench
items.statement: The method of gaining local information about the cohomology class by comparing the global basis in which ρ_H(τ) is diagonal with the local basis in which ρ_H|_{G_p} is upper triangular; it fails if the two bases agree, so τ must be chosen with its eigenvectors distinct from those of ρ_H(G_p) for every p | p and every H simultaneously.
items.note: Mazur's name for the argument, from Ribet's 1976 paper.

items.name: Lemma 4.2 (eigenvector stabilizers have infinite index)
items.statement: Let v ∈ L_{m_H}^2 be nonzero and G_v ⊂ G_F the subgroup of σ with v an eigenvector of ρ_H(σ). If χ(G_v) ≠ 1 then G_v has infinite index in G_F.
items.note: Proved by building from the lower left entries c_H(σ) a class in H^1(G_F, C/m̂_H C(χ)) whose restriction to G_v vanishes, then using inflation–restriction, Nakayama and the irreducibility of ρ_H. The same construction is used again in §4.2 for b(σ).

items.name: Lemma 4.3 (a simultaneously good τ)
items.statement: There is τ ∈ G_F with χ(τ) ≠ 1 such that v_{p,H} — the eigenvector of ρ_H(G_p) — is not an eigenvector of ρ_H(τ), for all H and all p ∈ R.
items.note: Proved by an inductive construction of τ over the finitely many pairs (p, H) with χ(G_{v_{p,H}}) ≠ 1, using Lemma 4.2.

items.name: The representation ρ and its properties
items.statement: ρ : G_F → GL_2(L) is the product of the ρ_{H_i}, with L carrying the Λ-adic topology; it is unramified outside np; for l ∤ np, char(ρ(Frob_l))(x) = x^2 − T̄_l x + χε(l) where T̄_l is the image of T_l in T̄, the image of T in T_{(m)}; and for p | p, ρ|_{G_p} is conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal (χ η_p^{-1} ε, η_p), where η_p : G_p → T̄^* is unramified with η_p(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = Ū_p.

items.name: The global basis and the entries a, d
items.statement: Let T_m be the completion of T_{(m)}, m̂ = mT_m its maximal ideal, and τ as in Lemma 4.3. Hensel's lemma gives unique roots λ_1 ≡ 1, λ_2 ≡ χ(τ) (mod m) of char(ρ(τ)) in T_m; in the corresponding eigenbasis, writing ρ(σ) = (a(σ), b(σ); c(σ), d(σ)), one has a(σ) + d(σ) ∈ T̄ ⊂ T_m, a(σ) + d(σ) ≡ 1 + χ(σ) (mod m T̄), and then a(σ), d(σ) ∈ T_m with a(σ) ≡ 1 and d(σ) ≡ χ(σ) modulo m̂.

items.name: The cohomology class κ
items.statement: Let B be the T_m-module generated by the b(σ), σ ∈ G_F; it is finitely generated, by the compactness argument of Lemma 4.2. With B̄ = B/m̂B and b̄(σ) the image of b(σ), the relation b(σσ′) = a(σ)b(σ′) + b(σ)d(σ′) together with (68) shows that κ(σ) = b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ) is a 1-cocycle, defining [κ] ∈ H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})).

items.name: ϕ extends to the completion
items.statement: W is a complete local Artin ring, since m_W^{r_an+1} = 0, so ϕ : T → W extends canonically to a surjective homomorphism ϕ_m : T_m → W.

items.name: The characters ε_y, ε_{π−y} and ψ_1, ψ_2
items.statement: In Cases 2 and 3, ε_y : G_F → W^* is the Λ-adic cyclotomic character with π replaced by y: if ε(σ) = Σ_i a_i π^i then ε_y(σ) = Σ_i a_i y^i = 1 + ((ε(σ) − 1)/π) y, a finite sum because y is nilpotent and πy = y^2 in W; ε_{π−y} is defined likewise. Then ψ_1 = 1 in Case 1 and ε_y in Cases 2, 3; ψ_2 = χε in Case 1 and χ ε_{π−y} in Cases 2, 3.

items.name: Lemma 4.4: ϕ_m on the diagonal entries
items.statement: ϕ_m(a(σ)) = ψ_1(σ) and ϕ_m(d(σ)) = ψ_2(σ) for all σ ∈ G_F.
items.note: Proved from ϕ_m(T_l) = ψ_1(Frob_l) + ψ_2(Frob_l), the identity ψ_1ψ_2 = χε (which uses ε_y ε_{π−y} = ε and πy = y^2), and solving the two equations obtained from σ and στ. This refinement of (68) — that ϕ_m, not merely its reduction, splits as a sum of two characters — is what makes the final computation possible.

items.name: Remark 4.5: a lower bound for dim_E B/IB
items.statement: For I the kernel of φ′ : T_m → E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}), Lemma 4.4 gives a class [κ̃] ∈ H^1(G_F, (B/IB)(ψ_1ψ_2^{-1})), and the method of Mazur–Wiles yields dim_E B/IB ≥ r_an + 1: with J ⊂ Λ_{(1)} the kernel of Λ_{(1)} → T_m/I one has Λ_{(1)}/J ≅ T_m/I ≅ E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}), hence J = (π^{r_an+1}), and Fitt_{Λ_{(1)}}(B/IB) ≡ Fitt_{T_m} B ≡ 0 (mod I) because B is a faithful T_m-module, so Fitt_{Λ_{(1)}}(B/IB) ⊂ J. It is unclear whether [κ̃] can be used to construct r cyclotomic classes in H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})).
items.note: An aside, used nowhere else. The homomorphism φ′ named here is not the one constructed in Remark 3.4, whose domain is T′ and whose target is E[π]/π^{r+1}; see the source issues.

items.name: The local change of basis and the formula for b(σ)
items.statement: For each p | p let (A_p, B_p; C_p, D_p) ∈ GL_2(L_m) be the change of basis from the local basis of (64) to the global basis of (65), so that (a, b; c, d)(σ)·(A_p, B_p; C_p, D_p) = (A_p, B_p; C_p, D_p)·(χη_p^{-1}ε(σ), *; 0, η_p(σ)) for σ ∈ G_p; comparing top left entries, b(σ) = (A_p/C_p)(χ η_p^{-1} ε(σ) − a(σ)) for σ ∈ G_p.

items.name: Lemma 4.6: A_p and C_p are invertible
items.statement: A_p and C_p are invertible in L_m.
items.note: Because a zero projection to some L_{m_{H_i}} would make the eigenvector of ρ_{H_i}(G_p) an eigenvector of ρ_{H_i}(τ), contradicting Lemma 4.3.

items.name: Lemma 4.7: κ is unramified outside R
items.statement: [κ] ∈ H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})) is unramified outside R. Away from p this holds for any class, since the image of I_w in G_w^{ab} is pro-ℓ while B̄ is pro-p; at p ∈ R′ the class is even locally trivial, because some σ̃ ∈ G_p has χ(σ̃) ≠ 1, whence χη_p^{-1}ε(σ̃) − a(σ̃) ∈ T_m^* and A_p/C_p ∈ B, so that κ(σ) = (1 − χ^{-1}(σ)) A_p/C_p is a coboundary on G_p.

items.name: Lemma 4.8: B is generated by inertia at R
items.statement: B is generated as a T_m-module by the b(σ) for σ ∈ I_p, p ∈ R.
items.note: This is where Proposition 2.2 is used: the quotient class is unramified everywhere, hence zero, and Nakayama finishes.

items.name: Lemma 4.9: the size of B
items.note: From Lemma 4.8 and (80), using η_p(σ) ≡ ε(σ) ≡ a(σ) ≡ 1 (mod m̂) and χ(I_p) = 1 for p ∈ R.

items.name: The group ring elements σ_ij and the values of the class
items.statement: Let u_1, …, u_r be an E-basis of U_χ and write u_j = Σ_k y_jk ⊗ e_jk with y_jk ∈ O_H[1/p]^* and e_jk ∈ E. For each i put σ_ij = Σ_k e_jk y_jk^{(i)} ∈ E[G_{p_i}], where y_jk^{(i)} ∈ G_{p_i} is any element whose image in G_{p_i}^{ab} is rec(y_jk). Since χ(G_{p_i}) = 1, res_{p_i} κ(u_j) = b̄(σ_ij).

items.name: The r equations in B̄
items.statement: By Proposition 2.1 and Lemma 4.7, Σ_{i=1}^r res_{p_i} κ(u_j) = 0 in B̄ for j = 1, …, r; equivalently Σ_{i=1}^r b(σ_ij) ∈ m̂B for each j.

items.name: The local expansion of b(σ_ij)
items.statement: b(σ_ij) = Σ_k e_jk (A_i/C_i)(η_i^{-1} ε(y_jk^{(i)}) − a(y_jk^{(i)})), and modulo (m̂^2, I): η_i^{-1}(y_jk^{(i)}) = U_{p_i}^{o_i(y_jk)} ≡ 1 + o_i(y_jk)(U_{p_i} − 1), ε(y_jk^{(i)}) ≡ 1 + ℓ_i(y_jk)π (mod π^2), and a(y_jk^{(i)}) ≡ 1 + a_i′(y_jk), where a_i′(y_jk) ∈ m̂ satisfies ϕ_m(a_i′(y_jk)) = 0 in Case 1 and ℓ_i(y_jk) y in Cases 2 and 3. Hence b(σ_ij) = (A_i/C_i)(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)(U_{p_i} − 1) − a_i′(u_j) + m_ij) with m_ij ∈ (m̂^2, I).
items.note: This is where the two local maps ℓ_i and o_i of the regulator enter the Hecke side: ℓ_i through the cyclotomic character and o_i through the U_p-eigenvalue.

items.name: The determinant vanishes
items.statement: By Lemma 4.9, m̂B ⊂ Σ_i (A_i/C_i) m̂^2, so (82) becomes Σ_i (A_i/C_i)(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)(U_{p_i} − 1) − a_i′(u_j) + m_ij) = 0 for each j after altering the m_ij by elements of m̂^2; the determinant of the matrix with these rows vanishes, since its rows all sum to 0, and the invertible constants A_i/C_i cancel, leaving det(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)(U_{p_i} − 1) − a_i′(u_j) + m_ij) = 0 in T_m, with all entries in m̂.

items.name: The determinant in the Artin ring W
items.statement: Applying ϕ_m gives det(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)ε_i + n_ij) = 0 in Case 1 and det(ℓ_i(u_j)(π − y) + o_i(u_j)ε_i + n_ij) = 0 in Cases 2 and 3, with n_ij ∈ m_W^2; since every entry lies in m_W, the n_ij do not affect the determinant modulo m_W^{r+1}.

items.name: The computation of the determinant and the proof of Theorem 1
items.statement: Using ε_i π = 0 and ε_i y = 0 in W, in Case 1: 0 ≡ det(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)ε_i) ≡ det(ℓ_i(u_j))π^r + det(o_i(u_j)) ε_1 ⋯ ε_r ≡ det(ℓ_i(u_j))π^r + det(o_i(u_j))(−1)^{r_an+1} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} (mod m_W^{r+1}). If r_an = r then L*_an(χ) = L_an(χ) and π^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}, so L_an(χ) = (−1)^r det(ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)) = R_p(χ); if r_an > r then π^{r_an} ≡ 0, so det(ℓ_i(u_j)) = 0 and R_p(χ) = 0 = L_an(χ). Cases 2 and 3 are identical once one notes (π − y)^r = π^r − y^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}.

items.name: Lemma 5.1
items.statement: For p ∈ R and σ ∈ I_p, ϕ_m(ε(σ) − d(σ)) ∈ yW.
items.note: From Lemma 4.4: ϕ_m(d(σ)) = ε_{π−y}(σ) and ε − ε_{π−y} = ε_y − 1 in W, using πy = y^2.

items.name: The c-cocycle and its local bound
items.statement: Let C be the T_m-module generated by the c(σ) and C̄ = C/m̂C. The relation c(σσ′) = c(σ)a(σ′) + d(σ)c(σ′) with (68) makes c̄ a 1-cocycle defining [c̄] ∈ H^1(G_F, C̄(χ)), unramified outside p and hence outside R, since R′ = ∅ in Case 3. Equating lower left entries in (79) gives c(σ) = (C_p/A_p)(χη_p^{-1}ε(σ) − d(σ)) for σ ∈ G_p, and Lemma 5.1 makes the arguments of Lemmas 4.8 and 4.9 apply verbatim, giving C ⊂ (C_{p_1}/A_{p_1})𝔶 + ⋯ + (C_{p_r}/A_{p_r})𝔶 where 𝔶 = ϕ_m^{-1}(yW).

items.name: The proof of L_an(χ^{-1}) = R_p(χ^{-1}) in Case 3
items.statement: Repeating §5.1 with a basis u_1, …, u_r of U_{χ^{-1}} and ϕ_m(χη_{p_i}^{-1}ε(σ) − d(σ)) = ε_y(σ) − 1 + o_i(σ)ε_i gives det(ℓ_i(u_j)y + o_i(u_j)ε_i + n_ij) = 0 with n_ij ∈ m_W 𝔶, hence det(ℓ_i(u_j))y^r + det(o_i(u_j))(−1)^{s+1} L*_an(χ) π^s ≡ 0 (mod m_W 𝔶^r); since y^t = Wπ^t = (−1)^{s−t}(L*_an(χ)/L*_an(χ^{-1}))π^s in W_3 this becomes det(ℓ_i(u_j))y^r + det(o_i(u_j))(−1)^{t+1} L*_an(χ^{-1}) y^t ≡ 0, an equality in the one-dimensional space 𝔶^r/m_W 𝔶^r. If t = r this gives L_an(χ^{-1}) = R_p(χ^{-1}); if t > r then det(ℓ_i(u_j)) = 0, so R_p(χ^{-1}) = 0 = L_an(χ^{-1}).
items.note: This completes the proof of Theorem 1, since Case 3 requires the result for χ^{-1}.

items.name: Remark 5.2: a hole in Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack is filled
items.statement: The argument of §5.2 fills a gap at the end of the proof of Theorem 4.4 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, where it was suggested without elaboration that switching the roles of b and c gives the result for χ^{-1}. That is correct when r_an(χ) = r = 1, but when r_an(χ) > r_an(χ^{-1}) one needs the argument given here, and in particular the whole homomorphism ϕ_m; the homomorphism φ_{1+ε} of that paper does not suffice in Case 3.
items.note: Recorded as an item, not as a source issue against this paper: it is this paper's own correction of an earlier one, and the correction is carried out here in full.

routes.title: Arithmetic Iwasawa theory and the main conjecture, Part II: the Gross–Stark conjecture
routes.brief: A Part II of Arithmetic Iwasawa theory and the main conjecture for Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo, 'On the Gross–Stark Conjecture' (Ann. of Math. (2) 188 (2018), 833–870; arXiv:1605.08169). Let F be a totally real field, χ a totally odd character of G_F cut out by the CM extension H/F, p a prime, E the finite extension of Q_p generated by the values of χ, and R ∪ R′ the partition of the primes above p into those with χ(p) = 1 and the rest, with r = r_p(χ) = #R. Final theorem, as the paper states it. Theorem 1: L_an(χ) = R_p(χ), where L_an(χ) = L_p^{(r)}(χω, 0) / (r! L(χ, 0) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p))) is built from the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function and R_p(χ) = det(ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1}) is Gross's p-adic regulator on the χ-component U_χ of the p-units of H. This is Gross's Conjecture 2, the Gross–Stark conjecture; combined with the known inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r it makes Gross's Conjecture 1 unconditionally equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0. Cover, in this order: (1) the statement — the p-depleted L-function L*(χ, s) and its order of vanishing, the Teichmüller character, the p-units U = O_H[1/p]^*, the divisor group X, their minus parts and χ-components, Gross's regulator and its expression as a ratio of determinants det(−ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)), and both of Gross's conjectures; (2) the cohomological reformulation — cohomology unramified outside R, the cyclotomic subspace H^1_cyc(χ) and its dimension, Greenberg's algebraic L-invariant L_alg(χ), the orthogonality Σ_i (res_{p_i} κ)(u) = 0 for κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) and u ∈ U_χ with both of the paper's proofs (Poitou–Tate and the Kummer map; class field theory alone), and the injectivity of the product of the inertia restrictions (Proposition 2.2), which replaces the rank one injectivity that fails for r > 1; (3) Hida theory in weight one — Λ = O_E[[T]], the specializations ν_k, the uniformizer π = T/log_p u and the Λ-adic cyclotomic character; Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms, the ordinary projector, cuspidal Hida families and their Hecke algebras; the Eisenstein family E(1, χ) whose constant terms are the p-adic L-function, Ventullo's auxiliary family G, the cusp form F, and the trichotomy of cases R′ ≠ ∅, R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) ≠ 0, and R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) = 0; (4) the infinitesimal eigenform — the Hecke orbit of F modulo π^{r_an+1}, and the Λ-algebra homomorphisms of Theorems 3.3, 3.6 and 3.8 onto the Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3, in which the relation ε_1 ⋯ ε_r = −(−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} carries the leading term of the p-adic L-function; the dimension counts 2^r + r_an − 1 and 2^r + 2r_an − 2 that prove those homomorphisms injective; (5) the cohomology class — the Galois representations of Hida families after Wiles and Hida, the reducedness of the local Hecke algebra, Ribet's wrench (Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3), the class κ(σ) = b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ) in H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})), the refinement ϕ_m(a) = ψ_1, ϕ_m(d) = ψ_2 of Lemma 4.4, and the local study of Lemmas 4.6–4.9; (6) the computation of the regulator — the r equations obtained from the orthogonality, the determinant identity in m_W^r/m_W^{r+1}, and the c-cocycle argument of §5.2 that settles χ^{-1} in Case 3. Treat the step the paper leaves open (sourceIssue E1) as a proof obligation: the linear independence in Case 3 that completes Theorem 3.8 is 'left to the reader'. The statements the paper cites without proof (Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Theorem 4.1, the identifications used in the first proof of Proposition 2.1, the dimension of H^1_cyc(χ)) are separate items and say so. routes.reason: IntegralIwasawaTheory is the roadmap for this circle of ideas: I.3 plans the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function and its Hilbert modular Eisenstein input, I.5 Wiles's totally real main conjecture with its Hecke algebras, Eisenstein ideals and Galois representations, and I.6–I.7 the integral Brumer–Stark theorem of Dasgupta–Kakde, whose proof uses the same Hilbert modular congruences and the same generalised Ribet method. The Gross–Stark conjecture is a distinct theorem with its own machinery — Gross's p-adic regulator, the cyclotomic cohomology classes, the infinitesimal eigenform and the Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3 — so it is a Part II rather than material for the existing layers, none of which mentions it.

The complex L-function of the ray-class character attached to χ, its Euler factors at the primes above p with the paper's convention at ramified primes, and the non-vanishing L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 for totally odd χ. L0 owns ray-class characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars, conductors and local factors; L3 then builds the p-adic L-function that interpolates the values of this one.

The p-adic Gamma function, the Gross–Koblitz formula and the Ferrero–Greenberg theorem are the inputs to the case F = Q, which motivated the conjecture. They belong with the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-functions of a rational base; L3 already owns the branches, Iwasawa's logarithm and Leopoldt's p-adic formula, and Ferrero–Greenberg is the companion statement about the derivative at s = 0.

Three facts about Hida families over a totally real field that the paper uses without proof: a cuspidal Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion, so that S^o(n, χ)_{(1)} embeds in a product of copies of Λ_{(1)}; the localized Hecke algebra is reduced when the tame level equals the conductor of the tame character, because there are then no n-old forms; and its total ring of fractions is the product of the fields cut out by the cuspidal Hida eigenfamilies. L5 owns ordinary theory over totally real fields, including Hida control and the integral Hilbert automorphic modules these statements are about.
